newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rise in trade bent on mills.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rise in trade bent on mills.

text.p: Egypt share prices crept up a fraction in low turnover and quiet trading on Tuesday -- a day marked by the appointment of a new economy minister.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed 0.82 points higher at 350.68 points in below-average turnover of 42.36 million pounds ($12.48 million).

"It was slow today," said Tareq Lotfy of Intercapital Brokerage. He added that the reshuffle on Tuesday of the cabinet which installed Youssef Boutros-Ghali as the new economy minister had no immediate effect on the market.
"I don't think the market is sensitive yet. In the long run it gives an indication to foreign and local investors that the country is serious about what Egypt is trying to do," he said.
The reshuffle is seen by analysts as likely to help accelerate Egypt's privatisation and reform programme.
Alexandria Flour Mills headed turnover with 7.66 million pounds. Its share closed 2.49 pounds up at 84.99.
Lotfy said investors who did not get their shares in the initial public offering apparently paid a premium. "Institutions had limits of 85 to 86 pounds. But it never got that high.
"A lot of retail investors are selling at 85. Yesterday (Monday) a couple thousand shares traded were cancelled.
"Small retail investors might have seen the price too low and have sold today," he said.

The privatisation of Alexandria boosted share prices on Thursday when the state sold 1.176 million shares equivalent to 29.4 percent in the mill. The CMA had said the shares were sold for 82.5 pounds per share.
Also showing relatively good turnover was North Cairo Flour Mills. Its shares rose 1.5 pounds to close at 185.5 in turnover worth 4.58 million pounds.
The share was the most active in its sector on Monday.
"There was a block of stock available, but no interest on the institutional side. 185 pounds is cheap," Lotfy said.
"Institutions are diversifying their holdings and have started to be active in trying to catch the value early."
Commercial International Bank/CIB closed up 0.4 pounds to 72.5 pounds in turnover worth four million. Salomon Brothers recently gave a "strong buy" recommendation to CIB in an equity research report.
In the cement sector, most shares closed up, albeit fractionally. Suez Cement was the most active share with turnover worth 1.8 million pounds. The share slipped 0.24 to close at 67 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 475.75 points from 473.57 points while that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 260.57 from 260.19.
Of the 79 shares traded, 30 rose, 27 fell while 22 ended unchanged, the CMA said.
$1 = 3.395 pounds
